newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: RESEARCH ALERT - Colombia GDP forecast cut sharply.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Colombia GDP forecast cut sharply.

text.p: Santander Investment said it had cut its forecast for growth in Colombia's gross domestic product this year to just 1.7 percent from 3.0 percent and reiterated its underweight position on the country's stock market.

In a report entitled "A Rocky Road Ahead," Santander said Colombia's current recession, its first in 40 years, had "shaken investor confidence in a traditionally solid economy" and that political and economic uncertainty continue to cloud the equity market.

"We believe the economy slipped by around 0.5 percent in the first half of 1997," it said, adding that "less stringent monetary policy has yet to breathe life back into an economy purged by two years of high real interest rates."

As a result of what it described as "disappointing" output in all key sectors of the economy so far this year, Santander said it it had slashed its GDP growth forceast to 1.7 percent from an original target of 3.0 percent.
Santander predicted a turnaround in 1998, however, saying overall GDP growth for the year should total 3.9 percent.
As for the stock market, Santander Investment noted that the performance of Bogota's IBB index has been dismal ever since it downgraded the Colombian market froom market weight to underweight in May.

"We continue to believe that the Colombian market will underperform within a Latin American context and are maintaining our underweight stance," it said. It stressed nonetheless that a number of smaller-cap stocks, including Coltabaco, Banco de Colombia and Cementos Paz del Rio, continue to represent "excellent value at current prices."
